comments.body: Nit (non-blocking): a BZ2_bzRead call after BZ_STREAM_END does not fail immediately. If avail_in == 0 and f is not at EOF, it first fread()s up to 5000 bytes from f into the handle buffer (bzlib.c:1192-1200). Only then does BZ2_bzDecompress return BZ_SEQUENCE_ERROR. That consumes bytes of a following stream, and since lastErr becomes BZ_SEQUENCE_ERROR, BZ2_bzReadGetUnused can no longer recover them. Worth one sentence under side effects.

Nit (non-blocking): the BZ_PARAM_ERROR for NULL unused/nUnused also goes through BZ_SETERR, which overwrites b->lastErr (bzlib.c:886-890, 1235-1236). A retry with valid pointers therefore gets BZ_SEQUENCE_ERROR, and the unused bytes are lost. Same mechanism as the 'second call' case; consider saying so.
Nit (non-blocking): cite the man page by line, as elsewhere: `bzip2.1:230-234` (the -s entry, '2300 k') rather than '(`bzip2.1`, `-s` entry)'.

last.summary:
Approve. Only projects/bzip2/docs/surface-area.{md,json} change (git diff --name-only origin/master..HEAD), and `python3 projects/bzip2/tools/check_surface.py --only-docs` passes (24 public functions, 35 exported symbols, 23 macros, 2 types, 11 programs). The JSON has all 33 functions, each with parameters, errors, preconditions, postconditions, side_effects, no_stdio and source. Empty `errors` arrays appear only on functions that have no error codes (void internals, BZ2_bzlibVersion, the zlib-style wrappers that return NULL or -1), which is correct.

I checked well over five non-obvious claims against the cited upstream lines. All of them hold:
- BZ2_bzCompressInit: BZ_CONFIG_ERROR is checked first. PARAM_ERROR covers only strm, blockSize100k 1..9 and workFactor 0..250; verbosity is not checked (bzlib.c:157-162), so manual discrepancy #1 is right. workFactor 0 becomes 30 (164). With one bzalloc call when the EState allocation fails versus all three array calls before any free (168-187), the side-effect text is exact. blockNo is 1 after prepare_new_block (bzlib.c:125).
- BZ2_bzCompress state table (bzlib.c:407-464): BZ_RUN with no progress gives PARAM_ERROR (425). An unknown action in RUNNING gives PARAM_ERROR (439-440). RUNNING with FLUSH/FINISH falls through via `goto preswitch`. avail_in, not next_in, is compared against avail_in_expect. FINISH with no progress gives SEQUENCE_ERROR (457). IDLE is entered only on STREAM_END, and End sets state=NULL.
- BZ2_bzDecompress (808-858): no avail_out check. BZ_X_IDLE gives SEQUENCE_ERROR. Block CRC is checked at 830-831, combined CRC at 847-848, corrupt unRLE at 823. The verbosity thresholds at 826/829 match.
- BZ2_decompress validation (decompress.c): magic and block-size byte give DATA_ERROR_MAGIC (197-208). The checks for block/end magic (225-235, 591-599), origPtr (261-264, 497-498), nInUse==0 (283), nGroups 2..6 (288), nSelectors<1 (290), selector >= nGroups (297), code length 1..20 (327), N >= 2M (396), nblockMAX (358, 410/417/427), unzftab/cftab (502-522) and excess selectors ignored (299-306) all match.
- High-level API: ReadOpen PARAM_ERROR conditions (1103-1108). bzRead UNEXPECTED_EOF condition, including an empty file (1207-1209). ReadGetUnused ordering of the sequence check before the NULL check, and the lastErr reset that makes a second call fail (1231-1240). WriteClose64 step order: ferror on entry, then trailer only when lastErr==BZ_OK, then fflush, then free (1033-1085), and the corrected 'usual case is BZ_IO_ERROR, handle not freed' wording. bzclose's abandon retry (1524-1528).
- Buffer utilities: BuffToBuffCompress gives SEQUENCE_ERROR only for sourceLen==0 && *destLen==0, and OUTBUFF_FULL on FINISH_OK. BuffToBuffDecompress distinguishes UNEXPECTED_EOF from OUTBUFF_FULL by avail_out (1340-1345).
- zlib-style layer: the mode parser (last r/w wins, last digit wins, clamped to 1..9 when writing, 1405-1442), bzread's lastErr==STREAM_END short-circuit, bzflush as a no-op, and bzerror's positive-to-0 clamp (1566).
- bzip2: BZIP2 is read before BZIP and both go before argv (1841-1845). Tokens are truncated to FILE_NAME_LEN-10=1024 characters. Flags are handled in two passes, with the long pass overriding the short one. A lone '-' is ignored. -s caps the block size only when compressing. -V/-L do not exit. -c with -t exits 1. Exit codes are 1/2/3 via cleanUpAndFail/setExit (757, 770, 787, 801, 812, 875, 888, 902). The -f trycat path rewinds and copies the whole input (465, 506-517).
- bzip2recover: the 50000th magic match aborts, given currBlock starting at 0 and the check before the increment (398, 441-443). Names of BZ_MAX_FILENAME-20 = 1980 or more characters are rejected (378-383). writeError prints 'I/O error reading' (104-113).
- Makefile: bunzip2/bzcat are copies (79-80) and the scripts are symlinks (92-101). bzip2recover does not link libbz2 (43-44).

Speculative points are marked (uncertain) and collected in §10: reachability of the assertions, calls after an error, BZ_PARAM_ERROR from BZ2_bzWrite, bzmore's exit status, and Windows. The manual/code discrepancies in §9 that I checked are accurate.

The three nits below are non-blocking; fold them into a later edit if convenient.
